title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement: A rectangular box measures \(a \times b \times c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are integers and \(1 \le a \le b \le c.\) The volume and the surface area of the box are numerically equal. How many ordered triples \((a, b, c)\) are possible?

solutions.text:
Numerically equal volume and surface area means \(abc=2(ab+bc+ca).\) Dividing by \(abc\) gives \(1=\frac{2}{a}+\frac{2}{b}+\frac{2}{c}\le\frac{6}{a},\) so \(a\le6.\) The cases \(a=1\) and \(a=2\) give no positive solutions. For \(a\ne2,\) set \[ \begin{gathered} u=(a-2)b-2a,\\ v=(a-2)c-2a. \end{gathered} \] The equation then factors as \(uv=4a^2.\)

For \(a=3,\) \((b-6)(c-6)=36\) gives \((b,c)=(7,42),\) \((8,24),\) \((9,18),\) \((10,15),\) \((12,12).\) For \(a=4,\) \((b-4)(c-4)=16\) gives \((5,20),(6,12),(8,8).\) For \(a=5,\) the congruence of the two factors modulo \(3\) leaves only the valid pair \((b,c)=(5,10),\) and for \(a=6,\) \((b-3)(c-3)=9\) leaves only \((b,c)=(6,6).\) Thus there are \(5+3+1+1=10\) triples.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The condition is \(abc = 2(ab + bc + ca)\) with \(1 \le a \le b \le c\)
Show \(a \le 6,\) then for each fixed \(a\) factor the equation into a product equal to a constant
